subject.title: Synchronous transcript I/O scales with tool-result payload size and can block the event loop the liveness monitor samples

question: Should active embedded-run transcript persistence be refactored to an async or queued owner path now, or should maintainers first require a current-main performance reproduction before changing SessionManager semantics?
rationale: The source-backed risk is real enough to keep open, but SessionManager is a central persistence API and changing its synchronous contract could affect cache, repair, compaction, and lock ordering.

options.title: Require measurement first
options.body: Keep this issue open for owner-guided current-main liveness measurement before approving a broad async SessionManager refactor.

options.title: Sponsor async refactor now
options.body: Assign an owner to design and land an async or queued transcript persistence path with focused upgrade and session-state proof.

recommendation.title: Require measurement first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for owner-guided current-main liveness measurement before approving a broad async SessionManager refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent transcript writer seam work makes this the closest available owner for choosing the persistence boundary.
